title: The fall theatre season is officially upon us!  First up: ART starrin...
transcript: I feel like we all kind of forget that James Corden is actually like a really good actor. And with as much as people dog on him for films like cats and the Smurfs, it is easy to forget that he is a Tony winner. He won a Tony for Best Lead Actor in one man, two governors. And he is absolutely the highlight of this production. That's not to say that his co stars Neil Patrick Harris and Bobby Cannavale are not great. I thought all three were excellent. But James is very much the comic relief and gets a lot of the funniest moments of the show. There is one seemingly endless monologue that he does about halfway through the show that I don't wanna spoil, but it had me cackling and it even ended in a mid show standing ovation. That's how good it was. And of course some of the credit should go to Yasmin Reza, the playwright, who has written a really fantastic play. The play came out in 1994 and has sort of become a modern classic. And despite being called art and a majority of the conversations in this play surrounding one specific art piece, this is really a play about friendship. And that's where this casting, I actually think is most effective, because you really do believe that these three men could have been friends for decades. They have such a great dynamic together and play off each other really well. I Think without that, the play would kind of fall apart. But as it stands, this is a really solid production of a really solid play.
